caveats: **macOS release is not a genuine undo.** `unquarantine` reloads `/etc/pf.conf`, never the endpoint's prior ruleset, so any runtime pf rules present before quarantine are permanently lost; if the reload itself fails it disables pf, which is more permissive than the host started. This is why the capability catalogue classifies `quarantine` Irreversible on every platform.

**`whitelist` can isolate a clean macOS device.** pf has no per-rule granularity, so `add` and `remove` rebuild and reload the whole main ruleset, which always ends in `block all` and enables pf, whatever the device's current state. Running `whitelist` against a device that is not yet quarantined therefore quarantines it.

**Releasing the server record does not lift the firewall.** REST `DELETE /api/v1/quarantine/{agent_id}` and the console release end only the QuarantineStore record and stop the reconciler re-applying; the device stays isolated until the `unquarantine` action runs on it. REST `POST /api/v1/quarantine` is the mirror image and only records the intent, leaving the reconciler to apply it.

**Linux coverage is INPUT and OUTPUT only.** The chain is jumped to first from those two chains, so forwarded traffic and rules the plugin does not manage are untouched, and the plugin never calls `nft`. A host with an IPv6 stack but no `ip6tables` binary reports `quarantined_partial` because the IPv4 side is contained and the IPv6 side is not.

**Release replays state captured at the first quarantine.** The Windows pre-quarantine firewall policy and the Linux "ip6tables applied" marker are kept in agent storage, written once until a clean release clears them, so a repeat quarantine never overwrites a good restore image and a failed release keeps them for the retry. If no Windows policy was captured, release restores the Windows default (`blockinbound,allowoutbound`) and says so in a `note`.

definitions.description: Isolate the device from the network by blocking all inbound and outbound traffic except loopback and the whitelisted IP addresses (server_ip plus whitelist_ips, merged with the agent's own known server address). On Windows this blocks via the all-profiles firewall policy (not a rule) plus explicit per-IP and loopback Allow rules, covering both IPv4 and IPv6; on Linux it builds a yuzu-quarantine iptables chain, mirrored to ip6tables when the host has a live IPv6 stack; on macOS it atomically loads a full pf main ruleset via `pfctl -f` (never a named anchor). Waits up to 2s for any other in-flight quarantine/unquarantine/whitelist mutation on this device to finish before running.

Remove this plugin's quarantine containment and restore network access. On Windows this deletes the named YuzuQuarantine_* Allow rules and replays the firewall profile policy captured at quarantine time (or Microsoft's default policy if nothing was captured); on Linux it flushes and deletes the yuzu-quarantine iptables chain and its ip6tables mirror if one was applied; on macOS it reloads the system default `/etc/pf.conf`, falling back to disabling pf entirely if that reload fails. Reports release_uncertain rather than released when the teardown could not be confirmed complete, and on Windows/macOS this is not guaranteed to restore the device's exact pre-quarantine state (see the plugin README's Caveats).

Re-read the live OS firewall state and report the containment verdict (active/partial/degraded/uncertain/inactive) plus the current whitelist of allowed IP addresses when the device is not inactive. Always runs immediately, even while a quarantine/unquarantine/ whitelist mutation is in flight on the same device.

Add or remove IP addresses from an active quarantine's whitelist without fully releasing or re-applying the quarantine, reporting the resulting whitelist after the modification. On macOS there is no per-rule granularity: this action rebuilds and reloads the entire pf main ruleset (including the block-all default-deny) and enables pf, so running it against a device that is not already quarantined will isolate it.

description: Device network isolation (quarantine) with per-IP whitelisting
how_it_works:
`quarantine` isolates an endpoint from the network by programming the host firewall so that everything is blocked except an allow-list: loopback, the address the agent itself connects to, and any `whitelist_ips` the operator supplies. The agent's own server address is read from a value resolved once at agent startup, never at isolation time, so a host that is already compromised cannot steer its own DNS to decide what survives. On Windows it sets the all-profiles firewall policy to block inbound and outbound and adds named `YuzuQuarantine_` Allow rules (IPv4 and IPv6); on Linux it builds a `yuzu-quarantine` chain and jumps to it first in the INPUT and OUTPUT chains of `iptables`, mirrored to `ip6tables` only when the host has an IPv6 stack and the `ip6tables` binary is installed; on macOS it writes a complete pf main ruleset ending in `block all` and loads it atomically with `pfctl -f`, then enables pf and re-reads `pfctl -s info` to confirm. `unquarantine` reverses it. `status` re-reads the live firewall and reports `active`, `partial`, `degraded`, `uncertain` or `inactive`, plus the current whitelist when the state is `active` or `partial` (not for `inactive`, `uncertain` or `degraded`). `whitelist` adds or removes IPs on a device that is already isolated. Every mutating action takes one process-wide gate first, and a caller that cannot get in within 2 seconds gets `status|busy`; `status` never takes the gate. Every firewall command runs without a shell under a 15-second deadline (10 seconds for reads).

Deliberately not: a state-preserving undo on macOS. `unquarantine` reloads the OS default `/etc/pf.conf`, so any other pf rules the host had are gone, which is why the capability catalogue classifies `quarantine` Irreversible on every OS even though Windows and Linux restore their own prior state. The plugin also does not decide who is quarantined: the server does, and the plugin only applies what it is told.

### What you can decide with it

| Question | Action | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| Is this device isolated right now? | `status` | `state`: `active` (fully contained), `partial` (some expected rules or policy are missing, Windows and Linux), `degraded` (macOS only: the blocking ruleset is loaded but pf is disabled, so nothing is blocked), `uncertain` (the read failed or returned nothing recognisable, so containment is neither confirmed nor ruled out) or `inactive` (no containment found). |
| What can the isolated device still reach? | `status`, `whitelist` row | The allowed IPs read back from the firewall, present when the state is `active` or `partial`, and absent for `inactive`, `uncertain` and `degraded`. |
| Isolate it | `quarantine` | `quarantined`, `quarantined_partial` (on Windows and Linux: contained, but a loopback or whitelist exception, the IPv6 mirror or a chain flush failed; on macOS: the ruleset loaded but pf did not enable, so traffic may not be blocked), `failed` or `busy`. On macOS a failed ruleset load returns an `error\|pfctl load failed...` line instead of `failed`. |
| Let the device reach one more address, or stop | `whitelist` with `add` or `remove` | `updated` or `update_uncertain`, with the whitelist read back. |
| Restore its network | `unquarantine` | `released` or `release_uncertain` (the device may still be firewalled). |

What a "clean" answer means: `quarantined` and `active` show the plugin's own rules and policy are in place, not that nothing else on the host can talk out. `inactive` means the plugin found none of its own containment; on Windows a host whose own policy already blocks both directions reads `inactive` with a note, because no `YuzuQuarantine_` rule exists. Treat `uncertain` and `degraded` as not contained.

| | Windows | macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| What is blocked | Everything on all firewall profiles except loopback and the whitelist, both directions | Everything except loopback (`set skip on lo0`) and the whitelist, both directions | Everything entering or leaving the host through `iptables` (and `ip6tables`) INPUT and OUTPUT except loopback and the whitelist |
| What is not covered | Only what the Windows firewall policy governs; other security products are not inspected | Only what pf governs; other pf anchors are replaced, not preserved | Forwarded traffic (FORWARD is never touched), and anything done by nftables rules the plugin does not manage |
| On release | Deletes the named Allow rules, then replays the firewall policy captured at quarantine time (the Windows default if none was captured) | Reloads `/etc/pf.conf`; if that fails, disables pf. Prior runtime pf rules are not restored | Removes the chain jumps, then flushes and deletes the chain (and the `ip6tables` mirror if one was applied) |
| Reachable after isolation | Loopback, the agent's server address, `whitelist_ips` | Same | Same |

### Diagrams

#### Containment state

These are the five answers `status` can give. `uncertain` is a statement about the read, not about the firewall: it is what you get when the firewall query or `pfctl` read fails or cannot be parsed, and it is never reported as `active` or `inactive`. `degraded` only exists on macOS, where pf can hold the blocking ruleset while pf itself is switched off.

#### Isolate, then re-apply on reconnect

The server records the intent first, then dispatches. If the device was offline or restarted, the reconciler (a server background job that re-applies stored containment) re-applies from the stored record alone (never a caller-supplied value) and counts the device as confirmed only when a follow-up `status` reports `active`; a device it had already confirmed is re-checked with `status` first after a session change. The REST `POST /api/v1/quarantine` route only records the intent and relies on the reconciler to apply it; MCP `quarantine_device` dispatches immediately. The four quarantine actions are exempt from the dispatch gate so a contained device can still be released.

outputs_note: Every action writes pipe-delimited `key|value` pairs via `ctx.write_output` — not a fixed-position row like the collector plugins' `field0|field1|…` schema, so a caller reads by key name, never by column offset. A hard failure before any mutation is attempted (a missing/invalid parameter, a failed macOS whitelist-read prerequisite) emits `error|<message>` instead of the action's normal `status`/`state` row. Several outcomes also carry extra keys the declared schema below does not enumerate — `prior_policy`, `rules_attempted` and `note` on `quarantine`; `note` on `unquarantine`, `status` and `whitelist`.

privileges.grant: **None today**, since LocalSystem already holds firewall-policy privilege. Under the intended least-privilege model it needs Administrators-group membership or an equivalent firewall-policy privilege (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md`, row for `quarantine.*`)
privileges.if_refused: `state|uncertain`, note "firewall query failed - containment state could not be determined", result status `UNAVAILABLE` / `PARTIAL`
privileges.runs_as: Agent service account: LocalSystem today, not yet the intended `NT SERVICE\YuzuAgent` (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md`). Runs `netsh.exe`, resolved from the system directory, never a PowerShell cmdlet

privileges.grant: **None while the agent is root.** If the agent ever runs as a non-root account, each `pfctl` call is wrapped in `sudo -n --` and needs a NOPASSWD entry for `/sbin/pfctl` in `/etc/sudoers.d/yuzu-agent`, checked with `scripts/install-agent-user.sh --check`
privileges.if_refused: The capture's own `status` run: `state|uncertain`, note "pf state could not be read -- containment can be neither confirmed nor ruled out", `[result_status] UNAVAILABLE / PARTIAL / quarantine:macos_is_quarantined pf status unreadable`, `[rc] 1` (`docs/samples/macos.txt`)
privileges.measured: 2026-09-07, bare-metal, euid 501 (a non-root user), deliberately below the production identity
privileges.runs_as: Agent daemon as root: the shipped LaunchDaemon has no `UserName` key (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md`). As root the plugin runs `/sbin/pfctl` directly, without sudo

privileges.grant: Sudoers NOPASSWD entries for `/usr/sbin/iptables` and `/usr/sbin/ip6tables`. Under the packaged unit's `NoNewPrivileges=true`, `sudo` cannot escalate, so these grants take effect only on a unit without that setting. The dev installer script (`scripts/install-agent-user.sh`) also grants the `-save` and `-restore` helpers and a bare `/usr/sbin/nft`, which the plugin never calls (an over-grant, not a plugin dependency)
privileges.if_refused: A failed listing reads `state|uncertain`, with the runner's status forwarded. In the capture the first `iptables` read failed to spawn (the binary is missing in that container), and the note separately records that `ip6tables` is not installed: `state|uncertain`, note "ipv6_unavailable - IPv6 stack is up but ip6tables is not installed", `[result_status] UNAVAILABLE / PARTIAL / subprocess_runner:spawn_error`, `[rc] 1` (`docs/samples/linux.txt`)
privileges.measured: 2026-09-06, container, as root (euid 0), so the sudo layer was a pass-through and not exercised as a real escalation
privileges.runs_as: Agent daemon, unprivileged account (`yuzu-agent` on the packaged unit). Each `iptables` and `ip6tables` call is prefixed `sudo -n --` unless the agent is already euid 0

result_status.when: No `set_result_status` call fires on this path: a clean `active`/`inactive` `status` read, or a `whitelist`/`quarantine`/`unquarantine` rejected before any mutation for a missing/invalid parameter. Matches every sample's `[result_status] UNDECLARED / UNKNOWN /` line.

A genuine runner failure — the child process could not be spawned at all — on any read or mutation, forwarded via `forward_runner_failure` before the action's own status call runs — matches the Linux sample, where the first `iptables` read failed to spawn.
The runner's deadline elapsed (15s mutating / 10s read) and the still-running child was killed, forwarded via `forward_runner_failure` on any read or mutation.
The run was cancelled before it finished, forwarded via `forward_runner_failure` on any read or mutation.
The child (`netsh`/`iptables`/`ip6tables`/`pfctl`) was killed by a signal rather than exiting cleanly, forwarded via `forward_runner_failure` on any read or mutation.
A deliberate bounded stop: the runner capped output at its line limit and killed a still-producing child — not a failure, but incomplete.

result_status.when: `whitelist` on macOS, both `add` and `remove`: the prerequisite `macos_get_whitelist` read failed, so the ruleset rebuild is aborted rather than rewritten from an unproven/empty set.
`unquarantine` on Linux: a genuine runner failure, or a clean failure to flush/delete the `yuzu-quarantine` chain (and its ip6tables mirror), reported as `release_uncertain` rather than `released`.
`quarantine` on Windows, when the all-profiles policy set itself fails.
`quarantine` on Windows, containment holds but a loopback/whitelist exception failed.

`quarantine` on Linux, any non-full-success token.

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result.** Every action's output rows and result status travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore, queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`, like any other plugin dispatch.

**QuarantineStore (Postgres, authoritative).** MCP `quarantine_device` writes the containment intent through `QuarantineStore::quarantine_device` before it dispatches this plugin's `quarantine` action. The store holds at most one active record per agent and is not expendable telemetry: it persists until an administrator lifts it, with no clock-guarded retention. `QuarantineContainmentReconciler` re-drives containment from that stored record alone, never a fresh or caller-supplied value, when the agent reconnects, through the shared `redispatch_stored_containment` chokepoint.

**Not consumed by** daily-sync inventory, the Echo warehouse, DEX or metrics. Nothing runs on a schedule inside the plugin; it executes only when an operator, MCP `quarantine_device` or the reconciler dispatches one of its four definitions.

**Sensitivity.** `whitelist` rows, emitted by `status` (when the state is `active` or `partial`) and by `whitelist`, carry the quarantine allow-list as raw IP addresses, network identifiers that can pinpoint a specific device or server. The other fields (`status`, `state`, `rules_applied`, `note`) are counts, enums and free-text failure descriptions; none names a person or installed software.

**Siblings:** `rdp_control.set_state` shares the same Administrators-group-or-equivalent grant shape on Windows and cites it rather than declaring a new right (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md`, row for `rdp_control.set_state`).

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) then `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) then `discover_instructions` / `get_definition("security.quarantine.isolate")`. Run: `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`, or MCP `quarantine_device` for the record plus live isolation. Read: `/api/responses/{id}` for the instruction result; `/api/v1/quarantine` for the QuarantineStore-backed record.
